MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "In Absentia feels like a natural next choice after Tool because I want intricate, atmospheric music with heavier passages.",
    "Back in Black fits my interest in strong guitar riffs, while No Name Face connects with the melodic rock side of my listening reflected in The Reason and Seventeen Days."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "Violator and Bedtime Stories do not give me the guitar-driven intensity I am looking for right now, and The Beatles 1 feels too far from that current interest.",
    "St. Anger offers aggression, but its raw, repetitive sound is less appealing to me than heaviness with engaging melodies or intricate development.",
    "I passed on Demolition because I could not confidently identify the album from its title, rather than because I knew its music would not suit me."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My interest in rock seems to have been stretched to include familiar classics even when their sound is quite different from my recent listening.",
    "Heaviness alone seems to have counted too much; aggressive music does not automatically appeal to me without the right melodies, atmosphere, or song development."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My recent Tool listening makes progressive structure and atmosphere especially appealing alongside heavy guitars.",
    "I still enjoy accessible melodic rock, so my heavier listening should not overshadow the connection to albums like The Reason and Seventeen Days.",
    "The two Back in Black entries represent the same listening choice for me; liking one does not mean I want to choose both."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations recognized my interest in guitar-driven music but only partly captured the balance of heaviness, melody, and progressive atmosphere I want right now."
}
